sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Elden Throne** is a Site of Grace located within the Lands Between in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Elden Throne is the seat of the Elden Lord, the highest power in the Lands Between. It is a small court with a number of wood thrones on a platform connected to the Erdtree's entrance. These seats were once filled by the Demigods before their alliance crumbled in the wake of the Shattering. Only Morgott remains faithful to Queen Marika the Eternal.

The Elden Throne Site of Grace is unlocked after the boss has been defeated.

After Morgott is defeated, his curse if lifted and he reverts to an enfeebled human form. He reveals that the Erdtree's Impenetrable Thorns block the way inside, preventing even he from rising as Elden Lord.

Melina appears at the Site of Grace to offer a new quest: journey to the Forge of the Giants and use the Giants' Flame to ignite the Erdtree.

After the first cardinal sin has been committed, the area transforms into Leyndell, Ashen Capital. The Elden Throne Site of Grace is once again locked until Hoarah Loux, Warrior is defeated. The impenetrable thorns will be burned away, allowing access to the Stone Platform.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: is a concept referring to one's immutable, predetermined **destiny** in the world of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Flashes of light portended the futures of those who dwelled in the Lands Between. Fate emitted by distant stars was glimpsed and studied by astrologers on the Mountaintops; pale-blue starlight determined the fate of common men while Amber Starlight commanded the fate of gods, or so it was believed. The spirits of those who died in battle followed red lamplight through the spirit world to the Helphen, while the blue light of Usher of Death, Rosus, guided Those Lost in Death to the catacombs.

During the age of the Erdtree, the Golden Order fettered and suppressed the fate cradled in the night sky. Destiny was instead prescribed by the Guidance of Grace originated from Queen Marika, her Erdtree, and the Elden Ring. Grace manifested as golden rays of light, steering Marika's faithful toward their purpose. Later, Starscourge Radahn, mightiest hero of the Demigods, confronted the falling stars alone, and crushed them; the Starscourge Conflict sealed the very fate of the stars. His actions held his sister Ranni's Empyrean path in stasis, forestalling the meteor that shall strike near the Mistwood and open a path to lost Nokron, Eternal City.

sections.heading: Fates
sections.markdown:
- Destined Death is fated Death, particularly that of the Demigods.
- The Tarnished is destined to rise as the Elden Lord, as the one chosen by Torrent will break the Golden Order in search of the Elden Ring. Melina offers them this accord.
- Blaidd the Half-Wolf defied his fate by swearing an oath to Ranni the Witch, imbuing his sword with cold frost magic.
- The Cardinal Sin is the fated burning of the Erdtree. A Finger Maiden is destined to become the kindling maiden, sacrificed to awaken the dormant Giants' Flame.
- Malenia is fated to become a true Goddess of Scarlet Rot upon her third and final bloom.
- Melina is fated to become the kindling maiden or gain the Rune of Death to destroy the Lord of Frenzied Flame.
- Messmer the Impaler is fated to become the Base Serpent
- Millicent is fated to blossom into a scarlet valkyrie.
- Miquella the Kind's fate was St. Trina.
- Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze glimpsed the ruinous fate at the end of the Primeval Current.
- The blood-drenched Fingerslayer Blade only works in the hands of one who has been prescribed a special fate. It is proof of high treason committed by Eternal Cities against a vassal of the Greater Will, presumably Metyr, Mother of Fingers, long ago.
- Ranni the Witch slew her own Empyrean flesh to escape the path set by her Two Fingers, later wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against them beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
- Sorceress Sellen cannot die while Starscourge Radahn holds the stars in stasis.
- According to Count Ymir, the stars will guide the fate of the one who rings the hanging bells found at Finger Ruins. The Hole-Laden Necklace is the same color as Starlight Shards.
- Pidia, Carian Servant references his poor lot in life by labeling himself "ill-starred." He sells the map which marks the Amber Starlight at St. Trina's Hideaway.
- Lightseeker Hyetta and other would-be Finger Maidens of the Three Fingers feel a distant light guiding them towards their duty at the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- Traitorous Straghess's thirst for vengeance was such that it formed legs and stood of its own accord, becoming the Dreglord.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Bone-Like Stones of the outer god of Night hold the power to alter fate.
- Finger Reader Crones can foresee fate by studying fingers.
- After the followers of Sir Gideon Ofnir raided the Village of the Albinaurics, Elder Albinaurics prayed to the stars, night, and fate to punish every living thing.
- The would-be Finger Maidens of the Three Fingers feel a distant light guiding them towards their duty at the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
- The Eternal Cities used Starlight Shards to produce puppets.

sections.markdown:
- Godfrey, First Elden Lord narrated a cut version of the opening sequence. He knew the Shattering would transpire and summon the Tarnished back to the Lands Between. He directed the Tarnished to cross the Sea of Fog and claim the Elden Ring, the arbiter of fate.
- The link between thread and destiny derives from the (also known as the ), the goddesses of fate in Greek mythology. The Three Sisters subregion is a reference to this motif.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ensha**, also known as the **soulless king**, was a character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
King Ensha was a soulless champion with golden bones who claimed lordship over the Lands Between in ancient times. He was regarded as a hero to Those Lost in Death, who were always in desperate need of leadership. He held such masterful control over life energies that a single punch rendered his foes unconscious, stealing their vitality. His royal remains were likewise graced with potent restorative power, and so they were forged into armor.

The king's bones were later acquired by Ensha of the Royal Remains, the unspeaking associate of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Ensha's golden royal remains are set in bronze armor and decorated with crimson, cerulean, gold, and viridian gemstones, including a prominent red jewel on his forehead. His faded hair is worn in a ponytail and melted candlewax covers the besagew affixed to his right pauldron.

His golden bones are similar to Blessed Bone Shards, human bones imbued with the gold of the Scadutree—a blessing said to be the greatest honor that could be granted to the dead. Like the royal remains, these golden bones possessed healing properties similar to sunlight.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Erdtree Burial** is part of the central religion in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Erdtree Burial is a process by which Death returns to the Erdtree, performed in catacombs throughout the Lands Between. It was an honor reserved for heroes, as a proper death meant returning to the Erdtree. The remains of such champions were laid to rest in Hero's Graves constructed around the Greattree roots, which were once linked to those of the Erdtree. Some heroes, abundantly blessed by the Erdtree, simply died upon receiving their honors. Statues of Rosus, Usher of Death guided lost souls on their journey back to the roots.

Many different measures were taken to protect the Erdtree burial. Various stone golems, including Imps and Erdtree Burial Watchdogs, were used to deter grave robbers. Following the banishment of Lord Godfrey and his Tarnished, champions were driven from the colosseums and assigned as Grave Warden Duelists.

On the Night of Black Knives, a stolen fragment of the Rune of Death was used to slay Godwyn the Golden, the first demigod to die. As a hero, Godwyn was buried in the Deeproot Depths beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital, overlooking the Nameless Eternal City. Although his soul perished, his body did not, and his Erdtree burial enabled the Rune of Death to spread through the great tree roots, manifesting as Deathroot across the Lands Between. Deathroot corrupted the catacombs and gave rise to Those Who Live in Death, who defied the Erdtree’s call to return. At some point, either before or after the Shattering, the connection between the Erdtree and the Greattree roots was severed.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Expeditions** are the core gameplay loop in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Expeditions are deadly, three-day missions into Limveld undertaken by the Nightfarers of the Shrouded Roundtable Hold. They brave the ruinous Night's Tide to grow in strength for two days before challenging the Nightlord boss on the final day.

Matchmaking for Expeditions is initiated by interacting with the Table of Lost Grace at the Roundtable Hold. Select at least one Expedition and hit confirm. Each Expedition features a different Nightlord and is randomly generated using an individualized pool of encounters. For example, the Nameless King boss never appears during the Tricephalos Expedition.

Shifting Earth and other Events like Catalysms affect the runs.

sections.heading: List of Expeditions
sections.markdown: There are **eight** standard Expeditions:

sections.heading: Expedition Flowchart
sections.markdown:
1. **Day One: Noontide** — Nightfarers enter Limveld via Spectral Hawk; Night's Tide later restricts safe space
1. **Day One: Night** — Nightfarers are confined to a small area, fight a wave of tough enemies, and face a Night boss
1. **Day Two: Noontide** — Night's Tide fully recedes and the Nightfarers resume farming; random events occur
1. **Day Two: Night** — Nightfarers battle a second round of Night enemies and bosses before entering the Spirit Shelter
1. **Final Day: Noontide** — Nightfarers prepare for the final battle, and enter the tree
1. **Final Day: Night** — Nightfarers confront the Nightlord

sections.heading: Leveling Up
sections.markdown:
Nightfarers start every Expedition at Level 1. They can grow up to Level 15 by spending runes at Sites of Grace. Runes are earned by defeating enemies and bosses or by completing various objectives. Lower-level players cannot adequately wield higher rarity gear.

When a player dies, they are demoted a single Level and their Runes are dropped where they died. However, the deducted Level is not permanently lost; it is converted to Runes and added to the drop. If a player dies near a non-boss enemy, then that enemy will glow gold near its belly. It returns the Runes once it is defeated, even by other players or NPCs.

The Plague of Locusts raid event summons mobile insect swarms that temporarily steal Levels. The Sentient Pest is located somewhere in Limveld and can be tracked by observing where the insects fly after an explosion. The Sentient Pest is passive and doesn't attack. All stolen Levels are returned, and a boon that randomly adds runes on hit is granted if the Pest is slain. However, the stolen Levels are permanently lost if the raid is not completed.

This page provides an overview of the **endings** to Elden Ring Nightreign. There are **four** ways to conclude the game: *The Dawn*, *The Endless Night*, *The New Night*, and *The Night of Love*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Just like in *Elden Ring*, the player decides the fate of the Lands Between upon completing the game. There are three secret endings tied to specific Nightfarers, unlocked after progressing their Remembrance Quests.

The endgame sequence plays every time the Nightfarers clear the Night Aspect Expedition by defeating Heolstor the Nightlord, claiming the Primordial Nightlord's Rune. The Night recedes, revealing a memory version of the Roundtable Hold where the Primordial Nightlord sits shriveled and inert.

sections.heading: The Dawn
sections.markdown:
This is the default ending, available to all Nightfarers. The player returns to the Roundtable Hold and offers the Primordial Nightlord's Rune to a shriveled corpse, causing the rune to disintegrate. Soon after, all Nightfarers dissolve into Grace and scatter to return to their true bodies.

The Night is undone, and the Lands Between are restored to their natural state, with the Erdtree reappearing. A colossal giant is also animated by the Grace of Gold. This entity resembles an enormous Heolstor formed of wood and covered in fingerprints. Upon rising, the giant surveys the Lands Between, refuses the call of Grace, and departs into the sea.

sections.heading: The Endless Night
sections.markdown:
This is the Ironeye’s secret ending. Upon completing all of his Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Ironeye returns to the Roundtable Hold and confronts the shriveled corpse. Rather than offer the Primordial Nightlord's Rune to dispel the Night, he slays the corpse, thereby condemning the Lands Between to eternal darkness.

Following this act, cold ghostflame manifests within Ironeye’s right eye.

sections.heading: The New Night
sections.markdown: This is the Wylder’s secret ending. Upon completing all of his Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Wylder uses the Silver Tear to rebirth into Heolstor’s body. He becomes the new Nightlord and perpetuates the Cycle of Night.

sections.heading: The Night of Love
sections.markdown:
This is Recluse’s ending. Upon completing all of her Remembrance quests and defeating Heolstor, Recluse returns to the Roundtable Hold. There she hears the cries of an infant. Rather than approach the shriveled corpse, she follows the sound to the bed quarters where she discovers the Infant. She takes the child into her arms as the game ends, leaving the final outcome uncertain.

After the end of Expedition summary, the Witch of the Wheel offers her thanks where the Infant was embraced.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The hidden Wylder ending requires the Silver Tear to be equipped to the active Chalice.
- The Witch of the Wheel post-game interaction cannot be repeated.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Unlike in Elden Ring, players have only four options (and not six) to conclude the game in *Elden Ring Nightreign*.

FromSoftware **is a Japanese video game development company. Headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, founded in November 1986. It is best known for creating the Dark Souls series, Bloodborne, and Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are currently developing Elden Ring.

In April 2014, Kadokawa Corporation announced that it wanted to purchase the company from Transcosmos. The deal was finalized in May 2014. In December 2015, FromSoftware was nominated for developer of the year at The Game Awards 2015, but lost to CD Projekt Red.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: George Raymond Richard Martin **also known as **GRRM **is a American best-selling author and television producer. One of his most popular works is the book series "A Song of Ice and Fire", which has been adapted into television in the hit HBO series "Game of Thrones". Martin says that he always loved writing stories, and wrote many unfinished ones.

sections.heading: Elden Ring
sections.markdown:
Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has explained how the collaboration with Martin came to be:
 "I loved *A Song of Ice and Fire* as well as the *Tuf Voyaging* series, however if I had to pick a favorite I would probably say *Fevre Dream*. I personally see *Fevre Dream* as a masterpiece among vampire fantasy and had even previously recommended it to all new employees. Me being such a known fan of Mr. Martin caused our executive business director Eiichi Nakajima to reach out to him with the expectation that we would get turned down."

As George Martin recants:
 A few years back, Hidetaka Miyazaki and his incredible team of game designers, the creators of the DARK SOULS videogame series, reached out from Japan to ask me to help them create the backstory and history for a new game they were working on. Now, video games are not really my thing [...] but this offer was too exciting to refuse. Miyazaki and his team from FromSoftware were doing groundbreaking stuff with gorgeous art...

Miyazaki:
 [...] we were then given the rare opportunity to talk one-on-one with Mr. Martin which was an incredibly fun and stimulating experience. It was then that I strongly felt that I wanted to work with Mr. Martin.
 I am still unable to put into words how grateful I am to Mr. Martin for agreeing to our offer.

 Mr. Martin respected the fact that we didn't want him to write the game's story or the in-game text. Because we felt that would actually limit his creative output, [...] and then it would limit the inspirations we could possibly get from him.

 So we established very early that he would be writing that foundation, that historical element to the game, something that took place long before the events of the game itself.

GMMR:
 What they wanted from me was just a bit of worldbuilding: a deep, dark, resonant world to serve as a foundation for the game they planned to create. And as it happens, I love creating worlds and writing imaginary history.

Miyazaki:
 The actual collaboration itself begun with Mr. Martin ever so politely confirming what sorts of themes, ideas as well as many game-related aspects I had envisioned for the game.

 We started off by giving him these very vague and broad themes and ideas for the mythos that I had swimming around in my head. [...] Then he would come back to us with a lot of ideas: how about this, this, and this?

 This allowed us to have many free and creative conversations regarding the game, in which Mr. Martin later used as a base to write the overarching mythos for the game world itself.

GMMR:
 So I did my bit, and handed off to my new friends in Japan, and they took it from there.

Miyazaki:
 [The mythos I received] was nothing visual - they were all text. Rather than being a short story, it was something that depicted the setting or set the scene for the game and for the world, detailing the flow of history and the figures who appeared throughout it.

 These dramatic and heroic characters weren't really in our previous titles, so this was something that was really appealing to me - how he would depict the mystique and heroic qualities of those characters.

 There was, of course a story that came with this as a sort of backbone, but it played as more of an introduction to that world and a natural course of events for these characters to follow. [...] And then we were able to interpret this in our own way and provide visual to go along with that.

In response to questions about the project, Martin said, “Building the world of Elden Ring with Miyazaki-san and his team was a treat! The graphics, mythos, and action-RPG gameplay will deliver an unforgettable experience. I can’t wait for people to see what Elden Ring has in store for them.”

After the game's release Martin blogged:
 " Take a look at a few of the reviews:
 [...]

 “Once in a generation… masterpiece… beautiful and brutal… a sumptuous open world… ”

 Music to the ears.

 Of course, almost all the credit should go to Hidetaka Miyazaki and his astonishing team of games designers who have been laboring on this game for half a decade or more, determined to create the best videogame ever. I am honored to have met them and worked with them, and to have have played a part, however small, in creating this fantastic world and making ELDEN RING the landmark megahit that it is.

sections.markdown: The **Ellac Greatbridge** is a location within the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A massive stone bridge spans the Ellac River in northern Gravesite Plain. The Ellac Greatbridge lies southeast of Castle Ensis, beside the Run-Down Traveler's Rest. It can be reached from the Three-Path Cross site of grace by traveling north toward the withered willow tree, then following the road northeast.

The bridge is reinforced with barricades and scattered rubble, but its layout is straightforward. Proceed across until you reach the central span, occupied by Messmer Soldiers and lined with impaled corpses. Two nearby bodies can be looted for Ballista Bolt and Lost Ashes of War. At the far end stands a stationary Heavy Ballista loaded with Explosive Greatbolts. Sprint directly toward the siege weapon, dodging its shots, and defeat the Messmer Foot Soldier operating it. Once the threat is neutralized, return to the midpoint to collect any remaining loot. Proceed across the bridge to reach the Castle Front site of grace, where Messmer's army established a camp.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Gatekeeper Gostoc** is an NPC and merchant in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Gostoc is a servant working in Stormveil Castle, in the role of gatekeeper. Gostoc detests his master, Godrick the Grafted, who always looked down on and mistreated him. Gostoc prowls the castle, looting from the corpses of the Tarnished who die in their hunt for Godrick. When he encounters the Tarnished, he offers to signal the gates to open for them, but also suggests a hidden path around the outer wall of the castle which will allow the Tarnished to get in undetected.

However, Gostoc secretly planned for the Tarnished to die, so that he could loot their corpse. He stalks the Tarnished through the castle, stealing their left behind Runes any time they die. He also locks them in a storeroom with a Banished Knight, seemingly intending for them to perish.

After the Tarnished slays Godrick, Gostoc can be found stomping on his corpse, cursing him for the abuse levelled at him. Later, when Nepheli Loux becomes lord of Limgrave, Gostoc quickly becomes her attendant, giving him free reign to continue looting as he pleases.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Stormveil Castle
 - Gostoc can be found in the gatehouse to the left of the main gate. He will offer you the choice of taking the main gate or using the side entrance. Choosing "No, I'll use the main entrance" will cause the main gate to open when you approach it. This will not prevent you from taking the side entrance, however.
1. Stormveil Castle
 - *(Optional)* Upon entering a dark room in the western section of the castle, Gostoc will close the door, locking you in with a Banished Knight enemy. To leave, grab the Rusty Key and return to the door to open it. If you die in this room, you can return to it and loot the item without being locked in again.
 - *(Optional)* Gostoc will now appear in several locations around the dungeon. Speaking to him in one of these locations for the first time will reward you with a Grace Mimic. The locations are as follows:
 - Stormveil Cliffside. He will appear on a ledge above the Site of Grace, only if you enter the castle via the wooden scaffold and head straight back.
 - Western Wall ground floor. He will appear here after you have gone up the ladder past the door unlocked with the Rusty Key.
 - Chapel roof. He will appear on the roof of the chapel where you meet Rogier, after visiting the roof with the Grafted Scion and returning.
 - Rampart Tower. He will appear in the elevator tower, on a wooden platform that needs to be jumped to.
 - While he is in any of these locations, he will take 30% of the Runes you drop if you die in the dungeon. In order to get him to stop, talk to him at any one of the first three listed locations, and then at the fourth location. Then, return to his location at the gatehouse and talk to him again. He will no longer steal any Runes.
 - Additionally, he will become available as a merchant if you return to him after he begins stalking you.
1. Stormveil Castle (Godrick's arena)
 - After defeating Godrick the Grafted, Gostoc will appear in the room. After exhausting his dialogue his shop will be open once again. He will also stop stealing your Runes if you skipped the previous part.
1. Stormveil Castle (Throne Room)
 - After completing Nepheli Loux's questline, Gostoc will appear in the back of the throne room. After exhausting his dialogue, his shop will become available again, now with an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone available to purchase.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Cut dialogue suggests Gostoc was to be revealed a son of Godrick and, by extension, the Golden Lineage.
- Much of his questline and content was cut from the game. He was able to compete with Nepheli Loux for lordship of Stormveil Castle after Godricks defeat. He would succumb to the process of grafting himself, however.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Flame Fortification** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 3,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Flame Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Fire damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 FP per cast.
- Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces fire damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *FlameFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
 TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameFortification}) ) 
 - For example, if fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
 TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
 TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as fire damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple fire negation sources.
- Flame Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Fire damage in the game, especially against dragons, fire monks, and Radahn soldiers, as well as while exploring Mt. Gelmir.
- Flame Fortification offers greater fire protection than Fireproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
 - The Fireproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.
 - Fireproof Pickled Liver

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants

- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Fling a small ball of fire with Fire Attack Power equal to 202% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 255% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 11 points of FP to cast.
- Costs 22 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 29 points.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 9.25.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 26%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of 45%.
- Although this spell utilizes the Giants' Flame, its power is not boosted by the Giant's Seal.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- An easy to use spell with very early availability that'll provide very good damage throughout the game.
 - Doesn't hold up as well late game since more damaging spells such as Giantsflame Take Thee and Black Flame (especially the latter's maximum HP-based bonus burn damage) will be more useful when FP isn't as precious and kill speed becomes more important.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Like Catch Flame and Fire's Deadly Sin, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
- 
- Flame Sling was formerly known as "**Feast Upon Flame**" during the Closed Network Test.
- Similar to the Fireball spell from the *Dark Souls* franchise.
- Patch 1.07: Increased attack power when charged.
 - The Attack Power of the charged version was increased from 240% of Incantation Scaling to 255% of the same.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Gestures ** are expressive animated player emotes in Elden Ring. There are 47 gestures in total, 12 of them are automatically received on the start of every new character and 35 are obtainable throughout the journey, however many of them are missable and can be left unobtainable until the next playthrough.

sections.heading: Gesture Types
sections.markdown:
There are overall three different kinds of gestures in Elden Ring, they are defined by how they influence the player's movement.
- Gestures that allow the player to walk while performing them.
- Gestures that lock the player in place until the animation is complete.
- Gestures that lock the player in place and can last for as long as they want until the player performs an action.

Some gestures my also hide the player's equipped weapons until the animation is complete while others won't.

sections.heading: Motion-Controlled Gesturing
sections.markdown:
On the Playstation versions of the game, players can perform gestures without opening up the menu through the use of motion controls, by simply holding the *Triangle* button and physically moving the controller in the designated directions. Which gestures are performed are dependent on which slot the players have put their gestures in.

This feature can be a double-edged sword though as players may accidentally trigger a gesture at inconvenient times due them trying to adjust their sitting position while at the same time trying to interact with the environment like doors and ladders, or if they want to use items equipped in their Pouch at potentially dire times like Flask of Crimson Tears. To avoid this problem players can simply unequip the gestures in the slots that are tied to the most common forms of movements.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The following Gestures are used to complete puzzles:
 - Erudition: As this gesture is used to clear the Converted Fringe Tower puzzle, missing it automatically makes the player lose out on it's reward of Gavel of Haima and Cannon of Haima. And while it is also used for the Converted Tower puzzle, that one can alternatively still be cleared with some platforming.
 - Extreme Repentance: Successfully performing the gesture mid-fight while physically close enough to Patches will make him forgive you and stop attacking. Failing to perform this gesture and dying to him will also automatically make him forgive you by the next time you talk to him.
 - O Mother: Use near the Marika statue in Shadow Keep to unlock the Hinterland section of Scaduview.
- Golden Order Totality cannot be substitute for Law of Regression to solve the statue puzzle at Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Many Gestures were carried over from *Dark Souls III*.
